artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define the group $\mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z})$ as follows. For positive integers $m_1, m_2$ and integers $r_1, r_2$ with $0 \le r_i < m_i$, suppose the residue classes $r_1(m_1) := \{r_1 + k m_1 : k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ and $r_2(m_2) := \{r_2 + k m_2 : k \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ are disjoint. The associated class transposition $\tau_{r_1(m_1),\, r_2(m_2)} \in \mathrm{Sym}(\mathbb{Z})$ is the involution that, for every $k \in \mathbb{Z}$, interchanges $r_1 + k m_1$ with $r_2 + k m_2$ and fixes every integer not lying in $r_1(m_1) \cup r_2(m_2)$. Let
$$\mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z}) := \big\langle \tau_{r_1(m_1),\, r_2(m_2)} : r_1(m_1) \cap r_2(m_2) = \emptyset \big\rangle \le \mathrm{Sym}(\mathbb{Z}).$$
Each element of $\mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z})$ may be specified by a finite word in such generators. The conjugacy problem for $\mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z})$ asks for an algorithm that, given two such finite words representing elements $g, h \in \mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z})$, decides whether there exists $x \in \mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z})$ with $x^{-1} g x = h$.

Question: Is the conjugacy problem in $\mathrm{CT}(\mathbb{Z})$ algorithmically decidable?
artifact.category_tag: Conjugacy problem in class transposition groups
artifact.status_search_result: The group CT(Z) generated by class transpositions of the integers was introduced and studied by Stefan Kohl in connection with the Collatz conjecture. Available literature on CT(Z) and the RCWA framework discusses algorithms for computing in this group but does not contain a published resolution (positive or negative) of the decidability of its conjugacy problem; the question continues to appear as an open problem in the Kourovka-style problem lists.

status_evidence.title: The Collatz conjecture in a group theoretic context (Kohl)
status_evidence.snippet: CT(Z) is the subgroup of Sym(Z) generated by all class transpositions; it is a simple group containing all finite groups.
status_evidence.claim: Defines CT(Z) as the group generated by class transpositions of Z, the setting of the question.

status_evidence.title: RCWA — Residue-Class-Wise Affine Groups (GAP package manual, Kohl)
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms are described for computations with elements of CT(Z) and related RCWA groups, but no general decision procedure for conjugacy in CT(Z) is given.
status_evidence.claim: No published algorithm is known to decide conjugacy in CT(Z); the problem remains open.
